## How Meta Web moved from $652 to $276 — and the catch {.smaller}

Two steps. The first is what you'd expect. The second is what we caught.

**Step 1 — σ tightening + windowed gate.** Narrowed Meta and TikTok lift-test priors from 30% of point estimate to ~10% (CLS literature default). Re-included Meta Jan 2026 as a wide-prior windowed test. Switched the gate from full-history aggregate to in-window. Meta Web moved **$652 → $466.** Convergence improved sharply (divergences 35 → 0, effective samples 268 → 2,218). Three independent diagnostics — prior-strength ladder, alternative saturation curve, alternative saturation prior — all landed at $466 ± $7. Prior tightness wasn't the residual driver.

**Step 2 — window-basis correction.** Worked the gate arithmetic by hand. The gate was comparing the model's **14-day weekly-rollup window spend** ($508,038) against the lift test's **8-day Δy** (1,128 conversions). Mechanically $450 — the model had no degrees of freedom to disagree. On a consistent basis the implied "true" iCAC becomes $257, and the residual gap collapses to ~$10–$70.

Applied the correction (scale each test's Δy and σ by `window days / test days`). Meta Web moved **$466 → $281 (Model 1) / $276 (Model 2).**

The honest read: a meaningful chunk of what looked like a calibration miss after Step 1 was an arithmetic basis error we owned. Step 2 is what closed it.

**5 of 7 in band** (was 2 of 7). Convergence clean: R-hat ≤ 1.005, ESS ≥ 2,094, zero divergences.

## Out-of-time validation — architecture + Model 1 {.smaller}

Trained on the first 79 weeks (2024-07-01 → 2025-12-29). Held out the last 13 (2026-01-05 → 2026-03-30). Computed weekly posterior-predictive against actuals.

**Why we ended up with an asymmetric architecture.** Model 1 has one OOT drift — conversion volume plateaued in 2026 Q1 while the linear projection has it growing. A single linear trend control corrects it. Model 2 has two divergent drifts — same plateau, plus a sustained +4% elevation in LTV-per-conversion that *offsets* the plateau, not compounds it. One coefficient cannot disentangle both. So: Model 1 gets the trend control; Model 2 stays on the calibrated spec with its bias disclosed.

**Model 1 result (with trend control on the OOT fit only):**

| MAPE | sMAPE | Signed mean | Over-pred weeks | HDI89 cov | R-hat | ESS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **16.13%** | 16.41% | **−3.66%** | **4 of 13** | **38.5%** | 1.0056 | 1,208 |

Inside the industry MMM 15–25% band. Sign flipped from the pre-fix +18.83%, magnitude inside ±5%. HDI coverage up from 7.7% to 38.5%.

*Caveat we want to surface up front:* adding the trend control shifted Model 1's Meta Web iCAC by ~$33 (12% of canonical). Published windowed iCACs are point estimates inside a ~±$30 band under realistic spec variation. We're being conservative about how tightly any single number should be read.

## Out-of-time validation — Model 2, honest finding {.smaller}

Same train/test split. Canonical specification preserved (no trend control). Live chart on the dashboard's OOT Validation page.

| MAPE | sMAPE | Signed mean | Over-pred weeks | HDI89 cov | R-hat | ESS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **15.13%** | 13.84% | **+14.96%** | **12 of 13** | 7.7% | 1.0036 | 2,098 |

MAPE inside band. Signed bias is one-directional and **outside** the 89% predictive interval most weeks — the model's own uncertainty doesn't contain its own bias.

**Why we kept this as canonical.** Every remedy we tested traded one problem for another:

- The same trend control that fixes Model 1 over-corrects Model 2 — signed bias flips sign, keeps magnitude (−14.00%).
- A two-stage architecture (project Model 2 from Model 1's conversions × elevated LTV-per-conv) closes signed bias to −4.59% but MAPE worsens to 16.5% and HDI coverage drops to 0%.
- Per-window prior rescaling — same trade-offs.

The choice was between a known-direction bias inside the MAPE band and a noisier prediction with worse coverage. We picked the version that documents the bias openly and leaves Model 2's posterior-predictive intact.

The +14.96% reflects an LTV-per-conversion elevation in 2026 Q1 the training data couldn't see. Closing it cleanly needs the attribution scope discussed in the asks.

## Baseline — why 67% didn't drop the way you predicted {.smaller}

You expected: tighter Meta Web priors → attribution pulls into the channel → baseline drops. It didn't (3pp drop, not material). Here's what's actually happening.

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Global baseline (Model 2, 93 weeks) | **67.33%** |
| In-window (12 union weeks across all lift tests) | 61.32% |
| Out-of-window (81 weeks) | 68.32% |
| Δ in vs out | **7 pp only** — modest windowing effect |

**The decomposition.** Per your Meeting 6 comment that Northbeam's attributed-revenue universe is ~65% of total revenue:

- **~35% irreducible organic LTV.** Paid attribution mechanisms can't reach it. Our model is fit on total LTV, so this share lives in baseline by construction.
- **~32 pp missed paid attribution.** Largely Meta Web view-through credit. The lift prior shifted Meta Web's iCAC level ($466 → $281), but did not redistribute attribution into the test window — the spend-to-conversion coupling is view-through-mediated and invisible to our regressors.

The <20% target was framed against the attributed-revenue universe. Different scope from total LTV. By construction, the model can't reach it on the data it's fit on today.

## Per-channel concentration + apples-to-apples baseline {.smaller}

Per-channel concentration ratio = (in-window $/wk) ÷ (out-of-window $/wk). Surfaces what each channel's lift prior is actually doing.

| Channel | Ratio | Read |
|---|---:|---|
| **meta_ios** | **2.35x** | Well-fit — prior bites *and* redistributes attribution into the window |
| tiktok_web | 1.61x | Moderate |
| meta_android | 1.56x | Moderate |
| ctv | 1.11x | Slight concentration |
| **meta_web** | **1.04x** | Flat — level shifted $466 → $281 but attribution did not redistribute. The view-through fingerprint. |
| tiktok_android | 0.96x | Flat |
| **tiktok_ios** | **0.79x** | **Inverse** — channel contributes *more* outside its window than during. Pacing confound, not prior-tightness. |

Meta Web's 1.04x is the in-model fingerprint of your own Meeting 6 diagnosis — view-through credit invisible to the regressors. Reviewer challenge we want to acknowledge: the saturation curve or the windowed prior shape itself can also produce a flat ratio. View-through is the most likely mechanism but not the only one consistent with 1.04x.

**Apples-to-apples baseline on the attributed-revenue universe (the scope your target was framed against):**

| Assumed organic | Baseline on attributed universe |
|---|---|
| 30% | 53.33% |
| **35% (your Meeting 6 anchor)** | **49.74%** |
| 40% | 45.55% |

Cite as a band — **~50% point, 45–53% range**. Still above 20%; the gap is the missed-paid-attribution component, not a model-spec issue.

## Blocking — two questions we need answered today {.smaller}

### 1. Attribution-feed access

Can Kikoff share a Northbeam attributed-revenue CSV — weekly attributed LTV by channel, 2024-07 → 2026-03 (daily also fine, we'll aggregate)?

- Refits the model on the same universe your <20% baseline target was framed against. Today's 67% isn't comparable to your target by construction.
- ~1 sprint to refit and re-report on attributed scope. Inside Phase 2 deadline if data lands in the next ~5 days.
- Cost of no answer: baseline conversation stays on the apples-to-oranges 67% number, with the ~50% reframe as our defensible estimate.

### 2. May 2025 Meta Web lift-test spend-basis

The CSV cell shows $176,972 over 8 days. Two interpretations:

| | Implies | Empirical |
|---|---|---|
| **Option 1 (working assumption)** — channel-level Meta Web, 88%/12% treatment-vs-holdout | $276 stands | 8-day actual Meta Web spend $214,096 ÷ cell $176,972 = **1.21**, matches 1/0.88 = 1.14 |
| Option 2 — one cell of a 3-cell platform test, 33% of platform spend | Requires ×3 scaling; Meta Web drops to **~$86** (over-corrected); calibration re-opens | Would expect ratio ≈ 3.0, not 1.21 |

Evidence favors Option 1. We need your confirmation to lock it.

## Three judgment calls — your read shapes Phase 2 close {.smaller}

### 1. Meta Web $69 above the truth-band upper

Model at $276. Truth band $107–$207. Inside your safety range $107–$300. Diagnostic plans on file (saturation curve sensitivity, OVB from the 12 untested channels). Pursue further, or document and ship?

### 2. TikTok iOS $288 vs truth $109

Concentration ratio 0.79x (inverse) suggests pacing confound rather than a prior issue. Tightening TikTok iOS σ in isolation risks contaminating other channels' iCACs (we have evidence the ±$30 spec-variation band is real). Document as structural limitation, or attempt remediation?

### 3. Model 2 +14.96% OOT over-prediction

Inside the industry 15–25% MAPE band. One remediation slot held: Model 2 with both a trend control and an LTV-per-conv regressor. ~25 min of MCMC; carries a known calibration-noise risk on Model 2 iCACs. Try before freeze, or ship with the bias openly documented?
